title: Rainwater Harvesting
description: Capturing rainwater at the point it falls — from rooftops, fields, and ponds — to recharge aquifers and reduce runoff. Techniques include rooftop collection tanks, check dams, and percolation pits.
stat: A 100m² rooftop can collect ~80,000 litres per monsoon season
impact: Can raise water table by 0.5–2 metres in 3–5 years

title: Drip Irrigation
description: Delivers water directly to the root zone through a network of pipes and emitters, reducing evaporation and runoff. Uses 30–50% less water than flood irrigation while maintaining or improving crop yields.
stat: India irrigates ~10 million hectares via micro-irrigation
impact: Saves up to 50% water vs. flood irrigation

title: Crop Pattern Shift
description: Replacing water-intensive crops (like paddy and sugarcane in semi-arid zones) with less thirsty alternatives such as millets, pulses, or oilseeds. A 10% shift from paddy to millet can save billions of litres annually.
stat: Paddy needs ~1,400 litres per kg; millet needs ~300 litres
impact: Could reduce agricultural water demand by 15–25%

title: Atal Bhujal Yojana
description: India's flagship groundwater management programme, covering 8,353 Gram Panchayats across 7 states (Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh). Uses community-based management and digital monitoring to cut over-extraction.
impact: Targets 35% reduction in groundwater extraction in project areas
